nodes.label: Cover cropping methods

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: When was the cover crop sown?
nodes.answer: The cover crop was sown in September 2021.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: When are cover crops typically grown?
nodes.answer: Cover crops are mostly grown during autumn and winter, in the time between main crops.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Why are cover crops important in organic farming systems?
nodes.answer: Cover crops, including legumes, contribute significantly to the nitrogen input for main crops in organic farming systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How can the problem of high moisture content in cover crops be addressed?
nodes.answer: The problem can be combated by co-ensiling cover crops with straw.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_004
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What were the components of the cover crops mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The cover crops were a mixture of clover and ryegrass.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_005
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How are cover crops typically utilized in relation to the main crop?
nodes.answer: Cover crops are sown either around the same time as the main crop (under-sowing) or immediately after the harvest of the main crop.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What happens to the biomass of cover crops after they are sown?
nodes.answer: The biomass of cover crops is generally left in the field to decompose, releasing nutrients for the succeeding crop.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_007
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are the environmental benefits of harvesting cover crops mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Harvesting cover crops can lead to avoided emissions of ammonia and nitrous oxide during their decomposition in the field and prevent nitrate leaching that occurs during periods of low crop demand.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Conservation farming|Cover cropping methods_qna_008
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How often was weeding conducted in the experimental plots?
nodes.answer: Weeding was conducted three times a year in April, July, and September.
